messages:
alex_custsuccess: FYI — BrightCart (dedicated) just escalated. During a 3–4m marketing burst they saw persistent 429s and high end-to-end latency. They claim autoscaler never added nodes fast enough; min_replicas=2, max=20. Customer says requests queued for ~90s.

maya_support: copying their repro steps from the ticket: small concurrent burst ~120 rps for 3m, each request is a single-turn text generation (~256 tokens). They reported 429 spikes around minute 1 and sustained errors until ~minute 4. They attached our SDK logs showing repeated "rate_limit" style backoffs.

sam_oncall: ops alert fired at 4311112255: /dedicated/pool-B handled 95% capacity then 429s. Quick check — scheduling looked healthy but there were a few imagepull backoffs in that window and a couple of probe timeouts. Could be slow pod startup + registry pull.

jordan_eng_platform: Can you paste a short reproducer curl or payload? Also need kube events & pod describe for the timeframe. If the warm chain wasn't primed we might see slow spinups.

alex_custsuccess: Reproducer from customer (they ran this from a k6 script):

```bash
for i in {1..120}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":256}' &
done
wait
```

They said traffic ramps instantly instead of gradual.

maya_support: Customer logs (excerpt):

```
[2026-02-14T14:01:22Z] 429 GET /v1/generate  path=/v1/generate reason=scale_limit
[2026-02-14T14:01:28Z] backoff=exponential attempt=3
[2026-02-14T14:02:30Z] 200 GET /v1/generate latency=1200ms
[2026-02-14T14:03:05Z] 429 GET /v1/generate reason=queue_full
```

sam_oncall: OK, a few quick mitigations we can suggest to the customer immediately: 1) increase min_replicas to 4 temporarily, 2) enable a short warm pool (if not already), 3) add client-side jitter on ramp-up. I'll also spin up a reserve pod in pool-B to test.

ops_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4778 — "BrightCart dedicated slow scale-up". Pager duty alerted. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-4778 :rotating_light:

jordan_eng_platform: From platform side, things to collect:
- kube events for nodes/pods during 14:00–14:06
- `kubectl describe pod <pod>` for any pods that failed to become Ready
- registry pull metrics (401/403/429 from registry)
- autoscaler decision logs and probe timeouts
- scheduler bind latencies

Put command snippets:
```bash
kubectl get events --since-time=2026-02-14T13:58:00Z -n dedicated-pool-B
kubectl get pods -o wide -n dedicated-pool-B --sort-by=.status.startTime
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n dedicated-pool-B
# autoscaler logs (cluster side):
journalctl -u redwood-autoscaler --since "2026-02-14" | grep "pool-B"
```

maya_support: Noted — customer also hinted they rotated API keys around the same time (we saw a failed auth event) which might have caused probe failures if init containers hit the registry with bad creds. Could be a token rotation + burst timing issue.

sam_oncall: Two probable contributing factors: slow image pulls (registry auth), and probe suppression due to rate caps — leads to missed probes and delayed scale decisions. Also check if min_replicas floor prevented fast vertical ramp because pods were being scheduled but failing readiness and thus not counted.

alex_custsuccess: Customer is asking for a timeline and an immediate ETA to fix. I told them we'd try a config change now (min_replicas bump) and follow up with root cause.

jordan_eng_platform: Action plan:
- Immediate: sam to request temporary min_replicas=4 for pool-B and enable warm_pool=on for next 24h.
- Collect: platform to fetch autoscaler decision logs + kube events (assigned to me).
- Deeper: if registry auth failures show up, engage eng-infra for registry creds rotation fix.
- Follow-up: recreate load locally with same ramp to reproduce and test mitigation.

sam_oncall: Done — requested min_replicas bump via ops ticket at 4311112290. If customer agrees, we can also route their production traffic to a pre-warmed pool for next 6h.

deploy_bot: Rollout event: warmpool toggle requested for pool-B by sam_oncall at 4311112305.

maya_support: I'll email BrightCart with the temporary mitigation steps and ask for exact SDK logs and the time range. Also requesting their consent for us to mirror the burst in our staging.

alex_custsuccess: Customer accepted the temporary change. They're asking that we include a post-mortem and if we can provide recommended SDK ramp patterns.

jordan_eng_platform: Will collect logs and post updates in INC-2026-4778. If anyone finds a smoking gun (probe 429s, imagepull 403s, scheduler bind >5s) paste snippet here.

sam_oncall: Quick note for triage: look for these strings in autoscaler logs: `probe_rate_limited`, `image_pull_backoff`, `pod_unready_count_inc`, `scheduler_bind_latency`.

ops_bot: INC-2026-4778 status: acknowledged -> in_progress (assigned: jordan_eng_platform, sam_oncall).

maya_support: thanks all — I'll keep the customer updated and collect their requested artifacts. :eyes:

alex_custsuccess: Thanks team. Will update ticket and mark customer call scheduled for 16:00 UTC to walk through timeline and next steps. :calendar:
